newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES EXTEND GAINS, OUTLOOK MIXED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES EXTEND GAINS, OUTLOOK MIXED.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the third session running but analysts were divided on the subsequent market direction after the buying in continuous trade that followed the stronger selling after price-fixing.
Some analysts said last week's news of good March company earnings and low inflation then of 0.8 percent would keep the market mood good after recent gains.

"There could be a horizontal trend but I don't expect a fall," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage. Other analysts said this week's busy primary market could draw cash from the bourse.
This week non-ferrous metals trader and producer Impexmetal sells shares worth 222 million zlotys.
"Impexmetal is a really big offering... nearly twice as big as (Celuloza) Swiecie," said Pawel Demczuk of Wood & Company.
Celuloza had 7.5 million shares sold by the state treasury at a special bourse session Tuesday at 20.5 zlotys against the minimum price of 15 zlotys. The offer was heavily oversubcribed.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.5 percent to 16,721.4 points and turnover eased 4.8 percent to 174.9 million zlotys on all three markets.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of top gainer Budimex, up 9.8 percent in heavy trade, but said the firm might still be benefiting from a recent accumulate recommendation from Merrill Lynch.
Other builders did well on Tuesday, all seen gaining from the current uptrend on the construction market.
Mostostal Gdansk rose 6.5 percent, Remak 4.2 percent and Mostostal Export 3.8 percent, all also seen helped by recent strong earnings reports.
